transcript: Last night, my friend Sylvia and I went to see How To Dance In Ohio on Broadway. This new musical is based on a documentary of the same name following a group of young autistic adults as they prepare for a spring formal. As far as autistic representation goes, there are two things I noticed this production did really well. One, all of the autistic characters are played by autistic actors. And two, the autistic characters are differentiated enough from one another to avoid a homogeneous portrayal of autism. The actual material I thought was fine, certainly has some great songs but not the most original score I've heard. The books and lyrics were hit or miss for me but I did like how the show addresses commonly ill-informed stereotypes and discourse around autism, without getting preachy. Any “messages” are incorporated into the plot tastefully and in ways that make sense for the characters. Other highlights of this production for me included the fantastic lighting design and Liam Pearce as Drew. His voice, particularly his vibrato, just really scratches my brain in all the right ways. Overall, not a perfect show, but it's always exciting to see original and personal stories being told on Broadway. So I hope the show resonates with audiences, specifically the autistic community. With that another playbill for my collection.
